title.narrative: Community-driven and climate-smart rehabilitation of communal shelters and WASH infrastructures in flood-affected areas of Myanmar

description.narrative: The objective of this project is to provide and improve access to safe shelter and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities/infrastructure through emergency rehabilitation and reconstruction of community flood and cyclone shelters and small-scale WASH infrastructure. With this funding, building on the CERF-MMR-24-RR-IOM-33951 project, IOM aims to target populations affected by Typhoon Yagi and seasonal flooding in Mandalay and Shan South, which were hard hit by floods and heavy rains, with 396,000 and 86,000 affected individuals respectively as of 26 September 2024 (OCHA) and significant damage to and destruction of buildings, infrastructure, and essential services. The damage, especially to drinking sources, sanitation facilities as well as communal shelters has exacerbated already existing humanitarian needs on the ground, especially with regards to access to water and safe shelter. Overcrowded centres with limited clean water raise the risk of disease outbreaks and increase the risks for protection violations. IOM will use community engagement methodologies to address target communities’ needs for emergency rehabilitation and reconstruction support. Prioritizing damaged community evacuation shelters and WASH infrastructure, IOM intends to reach 10,272 direct beneficiaries in four townships to improve their access to water and sanitation facilities as well as safe shelter. In collaboration with local organizations with established access to targeted areas, IOM will create or strengthen existing disaster response committees (DRC) and assist them in identifying, analyzing, and prioritizing needs. The project will facilitate village-level planning processes by providing DRCs with tools and technical guidance to conduct needs assessments covering the following: a) damages to and losses of communal flood and cyclone shelters and WASH infrastructures; b) communities’ existing disaster response practice; c) availability of climate-smart reconstruction/rehabilitation practice, techniques, and local materials. The findings will inform communal exercises to rank rehabilitation/reconstruction priorities. To ensure climate-smart approaches, the project will consider adaptation to flooding when designing the repair/rehabilitation of community evacuation shelters and WASH infrastructure in target villages with the primary intent of reducing their susceptibility to flood-induced damages. This may include deflection, draining, drying, and durability, using waterproofing and materials locally available and suitable for flood safety, installing a drainage system in the facility design, improving water storage by raising tanks or expanding community ponds, etc. The project will create women, child, and disability-friendly spaces to enhance the equitability of access to community shelters and WASH facilities will be designed to ensure privacy and safety for women and girls, including adequate lighting and separate sanitation facilities. Further, IOM will support community members in improving skills related to maintenance of community shelters and infrastructure and integrate Disaster Risk Reduction measures by supporting the establishment of community-based early warning systems, facilitating evacuation planning, and promoting disaster preparedness.As such, the project will provide access to safe shelter and WASH facilities/infrastructure for disaster affected communities to ensure their immediate needs related to WASH and shelter are met, and to improve their capacity to respond to or cope with flooding related to seasonal and cyclone-induced rains through the support of IOM and its local partners. To collect lessons learned, IOM will assist the DRCs in organizing village-level debriefing sessions where community feedback will be gathered to evaluate the intended impact of the project.
